_ai_assisted: AI-assisted: protocol structure regenerated with Codex under Edu decisions for #137 and #191; reviewed by Edu. Sources rewritten with Claude to cite the primary sources of the team treatment guide, checked against NASA OCHMO-MTB-001 and Gew et al. 2026; reviewed by Javi and Edu.
_integration_status: Activated for confirmed numerical findings. Immediate clinical-priority entry before measurement confirmation remains a separate owner integration; no numerical finding automatically establishes urgency.

route.source: App routing, no medical claim: an episode that is already a medical urgency starts at the urgent steps. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source.

w_red_flags.text: Sudden/rapidly worsening weakness, unsafe movement or new inability to exit, new intense muscle pain, breathing difficulty or loss of consciousness? The last two mean a general emergency, not proof of muscle loss.
w_red_flags.source: Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: urgency symptoms for muscle problems; breathing difficulty or loss of consciousness are general emergencies.

w_escalate.source: Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: at least one severe symptom, or a clinician-declared urgency, makes the episode a medical urgency.

w_report.text: Tell the crew medical officer. Review together your symptoms, any pain, your real exercise load and your strength trend.
w_report.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): exercise specialists monitor crew fitness and the exercise done in flight. NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): crews keep regular contact with their doctors. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: what to review together (symptoms, pain, real load, strength trend).

w_limits.text: Is the worsening unexpected, or does it stop you from completing a task?
w_limits.source: Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: unexpected worsening or a limitation in a task gets priority assessment.

w_exercise.text: Review strength and aerobic exercise load, technique and recovery with your exercise specialist; do not increase the load yourself. Review energy and protein intake with the approved nutrition plan.
w_exercise.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): individual exercise prescriptions supervised by exercise specialists. NASA, Human Adaptation to Spaceflight: The Role of Nutrition [2] (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/human-adaptation-to-spaceflight-the-role-of-nutrition.pdf): adequate energy and protein come first; protein supplements are not required.

w_end.text: Log symptoms and training daily; repeat comparable strength tests as directed; follow prescribed recovery plan after return. No training through pain, catch-up loads, supplements or drugs without medical advice.
w_end.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/) and Canadian Space Agency, Return and Reconditioning [4] (https://www.asc-csa.gc.ca/eng/youth-educators/activities/fitness-and-nutrition/return-and-reconditioning.asp): progressive reconditioning after return. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: daily symptom and training log, and things to avoid.

u_stop.text: Stop exercise and risky tasks, get to a safe position and alert the crew medical officer now. Do not repeat tests at maximum effort or wait for another sensor reading.
u_stop.source: Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: stop exercise and risky tasks, get safe, alert the medical lead; no maximal tests and no waiting for another sensor reading.

u_env.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): flight surgeons follow each crew during the mission. NASA, Hazard: Distance From Earth [7] (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazard-distance-from-earth/): Earth support is delayed at Mars. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: Earth contact required in Earth orbit and on Mars; on the Moon, care on board and the clinician may request Earth support.

u_orbit.text: Send the case summary to the flight surgeons (mission doctors); this app does not send it. Continue local care without waiting for Earth; the clinician decides any return or transfer.
u_orbit.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): flight surgeons follow each crew during the mission; return in the crew's spacecraft if an emergency requires it. NASA, Hazard: Distance From Earth [7] (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazard-distance-from-earth/): up to 20 minutes one-way delay at Mars, so crews act with minimal Earth support. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: send the case to Earth in Earth orbit and on Mars; local care does not wait for the reply.

u_moon.text: Continue local care in the habitat. The clinician decides any transfer according to clinical need, vehicle and resources.
u_moon.source: Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: on the Moon, care continues on board or in the habitat; the clinician evaluates any transfer by vehicle and resources; no automatic evacuation.

u_end.text: Clinician review and transfer of care are recorded; follow medical limits and recovery plan for the condition found. Return or transfer depends on clinical need, vehicle and resources, not just a sensor value.
u_end.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): return in the crew's spacecraft if an emergency requires it. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: medical limits, recovery plan and any transfer are clinical decisions, not set by a sensor value.

w_concern.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): in-mission muscle strength standard of at least 80 % of pre-flight baseline. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: a concern-level finding gets priority review, not automatic urgency.

w_priority_review.text: Ask the crew medical officer for priority review of the concerning finding or unexpected task limitation. A concerning number alone does not establish medical urgency.
w_priority_review.source: NASA OCHMO-TB-031, Exercise Overview [1] (https://www.nasa.gov/ochmo-tb-031-exercise-overview-2/): in-mission muscle strength standard of at least 80 % of pre-flight baseline. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: priority assessment of capacity and cause; a number alone is not an urgency.

u_local.text: Alert the on-board medical lead for immediate assessment and care to stabilize you; check for injury or another sudden cause. Follow the local emergency protocol without waiting for Earth.
u_local.source: Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: immediate on-board assessment and stabilization, looking for injury or another sudden cause instead of assuming muscle loss.

u_support.text: Has the local clinician requested Earth support while local care continues?
u_support.source: NASA, The Real Story About Astronaut Health Care in Space [3] (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/faq-the-real-story-about-astronaut-health-care-in-space/): flight surgeons follow each crew during the mission. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: on the Moon the local clinician may request Earth support (team decision on #191; keeps Earth support available where the delay allows it).

u_handover.text: Confirm that a clinician has reviewed this episode and accepted responsibility for ongoing care. Select Done only then; otherwise keep this task active and stay assisted.
u_handover.source: Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: a medical urgency stays open until a clinician has reviewed it and accepted responsibility; this is a crew acknowledgement, not an authenticated clinician sign-off.

w_review_outcome.text: Wait here until the clinician completes the priority review. Has the clinician declared a medical urgency?
w_review_outcome.source: Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: after a priority review the clinician, not a number, may declare a medical urgency.

u_no_clinician.text: Keep risky tasks stopped and follow your pre-authorized local emergency protocol without waiting for Earth. This episode stays open until a clinician reviews it and accepts care.
u_no_clinician.source: NASA, Hazard: Distance From Earth [7] (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazard-distance-from-earth/): crews must handle emergencies with minimal Earth support. Team triage proposal [P], no published primary source: while no clinician can accept care, keep risky tasks stopped, follow the pre-authorized local emergency protocol, and keep the urgency open.
